(Paris, France) | college = [[Stanford Cardinal men's basketball|Stanford]] (2021–2025) | draft_year = 2025 | draft_round = 2 | draft_pick = 42 | draft_team = [[Sacramento Kings]] | career_start = 2020 | years1 = 2020–2021 | team1 = [[Nanterre 92]] | years2 = {{nbay|2025|start}}–present | team2 = [[Sacramento Kings]] | years3 = [[2025–26 NBA G League season|2025]] | team3 = →[[Stockton Kings]] | highlights = * [[NBA All-Rookie Team|NBA All-Rookie Second Team]] ({{nbay|2025|end}}) * First-team [[List of All-Atlantic Coast Conference men's basketball teams|All-ACC]] (2025) * Second-team [[List of All-Pac-12 Conference men's basketball teams|All-Pac-12]] (2024) * [[Pac-12 Conference Men's Basketball Most Improved Player of The Year|Pac-12 Most Improved Player]] (2024) | medal_templates = {{MedalSport|Men's [[basketball]]}} {{MedalCountry|{{bk|FRA}}}} {{MedalCompetition|[[FIBA U20 European Championship]]}} {{MedalGold|[[2023 FIBA U20 European Championship|2023 Greece]]|[[France men's national under-20 basketball team|Team]]}} {{MedalCompetition|[[FIBA U16 European Championship]]}} {{MedalSilver|[[2019 FIBA U16 European Championship|2019 Italy]]|[[France national under-17 basketball team|Team]]}} }} '''Maxime Pierre Raynaud''' (born 7 April 2003) is a French professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Sacramento Kings]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Stanford Cardinal men's basketball|Stanford Cardinal]]. ==College career== Raynaud graduated from [[Lycée Henri-IV]] in his native Paris. Seeking to continue his basketball development in the United States, he committed to the [[Stanford Cardinal men's basketball|Stanford Cardinal]] in 2021.{{cite news|first=Travis|last=Branham|title=2021 French big man Maxime Raynaud commits to Stanford|url=https://247sports.com/article/maxime-raynaud-basketball-stanford-commitment-165390714/|date=14 May 2021|website=247Sports.com|publisher=[[247Sports]]|access-date=3 April 2025}} He earned a place in Stanford’s regular rotation during his first two collegiate seasons under head coach [[Jerod Haase]], gradually increasing his role and responsibilities. Raynaud’s progression accelerated following his sophomore year, when a shift in mindset and work habits became evident. According to the ''[[San Francisco Chronicle]]'', assistant coach David Berkun encouraged Raynaud to simplify his approach, increase his overall effort, and focus less on questioning, a change that translated into improved consistency and impact on both ends of the court.{{Cite web | author = Ron Kroichick | title = Finally proud to be tall: How hoops helped Stanford's Maxime Raynaud enjoy life north of 7 feet | url = https://www.sfchronicle.com/sports/college/article/stanford-basketball-maxime-raynaud-20190428.php | website = San Francisco Chronicle | date = April 28, 2025 | language = en }} As a junior during the [[2023–24 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2023–24 season]], Raynaud emerged as one of Stanford’s most productive players, averaging 15.5 points and 9.6 rebounds per game. His performances earned him second-team [[List of All-Pac-12 Conference men's basketball teams|All-Pac-12]] honors, as well as the conference’s Most Improved Player award. Following the departure of Haase at the conclusion of the season, Raynaud entered the NCAA transfer portal and explored other options before ultimately deciding to remain at Stanford. He withdrew from the portal and committed to playing under newly appointed head coach [[Kyle Smith (basketball)|Kyle Smith]] as the program prepared for its inaugural season in the [[Atlantic Coast Conference]].{{cite news|first=Grant|last=Grubbs|title=Stanford forward Maxime Raynaud withdraws from NCAA Transfer Portal|url=https://www.on3.com/transfer-portal/news/stanford-forward-maxime-raynaud-withdraws-from-ncaa-transfer-portal/|date=19 April 2024|website=on3.com|publisher=[[On3.com]]|access-date=3 April 2025}}{{cite news|first=Janie|last=McCauley|title=Maxime Raynaud’s return to Stanford has meant so much to him and the program|url=https://apnews.com/article/maxime-raynaud-stanford-transfer-portal-798234703e7c710558846da8c8d677df|date=28 February 2025|website=apnews.com|publisher=[[Associated Press]]|access-date=8 March 2025}} Raynaud’s senior season (2024–25) marked the peak of his collegiate career. He posted career-high averages of 20.1 points and 10.9 rebounds per game, recording 23 double-doubles, leading the ACC in rebounding, and ranking among the national statistical leaders. He was named first-team All-ACC and ACC Scholar-Athlete of the Year, and became one of only three major-conference players in recent history to average at least 20 points, 10 rebounds, and 50 three-point field goals in a single season, alongside [[Kevin Durant]] and [[Carmelo Anthony]].{{Cite web | author = Ron Kroichick | title = Finally proud to be tall: How hoops helped Stanford's Maxime Raynaud enjoy life north of 7 feet | url = https://www.sfchronicle.com/sports/college/article/stanford-basketball-maxime-raynaud-20190428.php | website = San Francisco Chronicle | date = April 28, 2025 | language = en }} At the conclusion of the season, Raynaud was also named recipient of the [[Skip Prosser]] Award, recognizing the ACC’s top scholar-athlete.{{cite press release|title=ND’s Miles, Stanford’s Raynaud Earn ACC Basketball Scholar-Athlete of the Year Honors|url=https://theacc.com/news/2025/3/5/mens-basketball-nds-miles-stanfords-raynaud-earn-acc-basketball-scholar-athlete-of-the-year-honors.aspx|date=5 March 2025|website=theacc.com|publisher=[[Atlantic Coast Conference]]|access-date=8 March 2025}} Raynaud graduated with a double major in Mathematics and Computer Science. ==Professional career== Raynaud was selected 42nd overall in the [[2025 NBA draft]] by the [[Sacramento Kings]] and signed a three-year rookie contract on July 3, 2025.{{Cite web |last=Taylor |first=Cody |date=2 July 2025 |title=Report: Kings sign 42nd pick Maxime Raynaud to 3-year, $5.95M rookie contract |url=https://sports.yahoo.com/article/report-kings-sign-42nd-pick-210423850.html |access-date=5 July 2025 |website=Yahoo Sports}}{{Cite web |title=Sacramento Kings Sign Nique Clifford and Max Raynaud |url=https://www.nba.com/kings/news/sacramento-kings-sign-nique-clifford-and-max-raynaud |date=July 3, 2025 |website=NBA.com |access-date=July 3, 2025}} On November 4, he was assigned to the [[Stockton Kings]] of the [[NBA G League]].{{cite web |date=November 4, 2025 |title=Kings’ Maxime Raynaud: Transferred to G League |website=CBS Sports |url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/kings-maxime-raynaud-transferred-to-g-league/ |access-date=November 5, 2025}}{{cite web |last=Struck |first=Logan |date=November 4, 2025 |title=Kings assign rookie big man to NBA G League |website=Sports Illustrated |url=https://www.si.com/nba/kings/onsi/sacramento-kings-news/kings-assign-rookie-big-man-to-nba-g-league |access-date=November 5, 2025}} After limited playing time early in the season, Raynaud earned a larger role following an injury to [[Domantas Sabonis]]. Beginning in late November 2025, his production increased, including a 19-point performance against the [[Utah Jazz]] on November 30, with 16 points scored in the fourth quarter.{{cite web |author=Jason Anderson |date=2 December 2025 |title=Sacramento Kings rookie sees ‘quiet’ side of Westbrook’s leadership |url=https://www.sacbee.com/sports/nba/sacramento-kings/article313276262.html |website=The Sacramento Bee}} Raynaud recorded a then career-high 25 points, along with six rebounds and three assists, against the [[Houston Rockets]] on December 4. Two days later, he made his first NBA start against the [[Miami Heat]], finishing with 12 points and 10 rebounds. Raynaud later confirmed that teammate [[Russell Westbrook]] contributed to his development during his first year in the league.{{cite web |last=Struck |first=Logan |title=Kings Rookie Maxime Raynaud Opens Up About Russell Westbrook's Impact |url=https://www.si.com/nba/kings/onsi/sacramento-kings-news/kings-rookie-maxime-raynaud-opens-up-about-russell-westbrook-impact |website=Sports Illustrated |date=11 April 2026 |access-date=19 April 2026}} On March 17, 2026, Raynaud recorded a career-high 32 points and nine rebounds in a 104–132 loss to the [[2025–26 San Antonio Spurs season|San Antonio Spurs]].{{Cite web|title=Kings' Maxime Raynaud: Sets new career-high in scoring|url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/kings-maxime-raynaud-sets-new-career-high-in-scoring/|access-date=May 14, 2026|website=cbssports.com|language=en}} For the month of March 2026, he was named Western Conference Rookie of the Month after averaging 17.9 points, 8.5 rebounds and 1.8 assists per game over 15 games, while shooting 59.5% from the field.{{Cite web |last=Anderson |first=Jason |date=2 April 2026 |title=Why NBA Rookie of the Month award could mean more for Kings’ Maxime Raynaud |url=https://www.sacbee.com/sports/nba/sacramento-kings/article315280108.html |website=The Sacramento Bee|access-date=10 May 2026}} Raynaud became the first second-round pick in NBA history to average at least 12 points and seven rebounds per game while shooting above 55 percent from the field as a rookie.{{Cite web |last=Struck |first=Logan |date=12 April 2026 |title=Kings' Maxime Raynaud Makes NBA History in Rookie Season |url=https://www.si.com/nba/kings/onsi/sacramento-kings-news/kings-maxime-raynaud-makes-nba-history-in-rookie-season |website=[[Sacramento Kings]]|access-date=10 May 2026}} His average of 7.5 rebounds per game in the 2025-2026 NBA season led the Sacramento Kings.{{Cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/team/stats/_/name/sac |access-date=2026-06-02 |website=www.espn.com}} Raynaud was named to the 2026 All-Rookie Second Team{{Cite web |title=Cooper Flagg, Kon Knueppel headline 2025-26 Kia All-Rookie Teams |url=https://www.nba.com/news/2025-26-all-rookie-teams-announced |access-date=2026-06-02 |website=NBA.com |language=en}}, becoming the only second-round draft pick named to either of the 2026 [[NBA All-Rookie Team|All-Rookie Teams]]. ==Player profile== Christie described Raynaud as a “''sponge''” for his ability to absorb coaching quickly, praising his game understanding, positioning, and defensive awareness. Raynaud himself noted growing on-court chemistry with his teammates: “''I know where I have to be and when… It’s easier now than on the first day of training camp''”.{{cite web|author=Tanguy Mantovani |date=8 December 2025 |language=fr |title=NBA - "Une éponge" : comment Maxime Raynaud a utilisé sa tête pour s'imposer en NBA avec les Sacramento Kings |url=https://www.eurosport.fr/basketball/nba/2025-2026/nba-une-eponge-comment-maxime-raynaud-a-utilise-sa-tete-pour-s-imposer-en-nba-avec-les-sacramento-kings_sto23248251/story.shtml |website=Eurosport}} ==National team career== Raynaud has been a member of the [[France men's national basketball team|France national team]], competing at several levels of their junior program. He was a starter on the French team that won gold at the [[2023 FIBA U20 European Championship]], leading the team in scoring (26) in their championship win over Israel.{{cite news |title= Raynaud, Kamardine and Yaacov put on a show, as France outlast Israel |url= https://www.fiba.basketball/en/news/europe-u20-2023-news-raynaud-kamardine-and-yaacov-put-on-a-show-as-france-outlast-israel | date =
